h1: De Capoc Resort Khao Kho — a minimalist loft resort where the infinity pool stretches out toward the wind turbines
intro: Picture this: sliding into the infinity-edge pool in the morning and looking straight out at the Khao Kho wind turbines turning slowly above a valley still wrapped in thin mist — De Capoc Resort is a minimalist-loft boutique resort in Thung Samo, Khao Kho district, Phetchabun, playing with exposed concrete, high ceilings, and 180-degree mountain-view balconies · the name De Capoc comes from French, evoking soft kapok down and the mountain mist · near Wat Phra That Pha Sorn Kaew and the wind-turbine field, from about THB 2,000/night · real guest reviews give it 9.2 on Trip.com and 8.7 from 1,394 reviews on Agoda

body.html: Overview and who it suits — to put it as simply as possible, De Capoc Resort is a resort for people who want the calm, design-led side of Khao Kho, without the crowds of the heavily themed resorts that open their gardens to day visitors · this isn't a flower-castle resort you come to in order to take photos all day; it's a compact resort of around 34 rooms that positions itself as a minimalist-loft stay in the middle of the Thung Samo valley · the name De Capoc comes from French, pronounced "de capoc," evoking soft kapok down and the mountain mist, which captures the concept of the place quite literally · it has been open since 2017 and is still running today, and it's one of the more frequently reviewed stays in the Thung Samo–Khao Kho area · real guest reviews line up on who fits here: couples who want a quiet, private corner, photo lovers who like exposed-concrete design and clean lines, and small families who want to genuinely rest rather than chase resort activities · another group that says they were impressed is people who drive up Khao Kho themselves and use the resort as a base for visiting Wat Pha Sorn Kaew, the wind-turbine field, and the viewpoints around it · on the flip side, if you're after a big resort packed with activities, a theme park, or every amenity in one place, De Capoc may not be the answer, because its selling point is simplicity, quiet, and the view rather than spectacle

Location and getting there — De Capoc Resort sits at 254 Moo 4, Thung Samo, Khao Kho district, Phetchabun 67270, on a hillside facing out toward the mountains and the wind-turbine field · the Thung Samo area is a zone between the road up Khao Kho and the cluster of popular sights, which makes getting around easy with short drives · the location point reviews mention most is that it's only about 1.5–2 km from Wat Phra That Pha Sorn Kaew, one of the top Khao Kho highlights that almost no one visiting Phetchabun skips · there's also Wat Thung Samo and a meditation center within 1–1.5 km · the Khao Kho wind-turbine field, Khao Kho Palace, and the Memorial Monument are about 15–30 min drive away · getting here is mostly by private car or rental, since Khao Kho is mountain country with limited public transport · from Bangkok it's about a 5–6 hour drive, and from Phetchabun town it's about 1 hour up · one thing to be prepared for is that the final stretch is a mountain road with some steep grades and bends; an ordinary sedan can make it, but drive carefully and avoid going up at night or in heavy rain if you don't know the road well
"Woke up early and slipped into the pool, looked straight out at the wind turbines turning slowly with thin mist on the mountains — it felt so peaceful I didn't want to go anywhere."

Room types and decor — De Capoc has around 34 rooms in total, split into just a few main types to keep the choice simple · the main group is Deluxe at about 42 sqm, the room reviewers talk about most, because it has a private balcony with a wide, almost 180-degree mountain view that opens out with nothing in the way · larger suites like the Deluxe King Suite and Suite with Terrace add a sitting area and a wider balcony · the most luxurious is the Villa at about 60 sqm, whose standout features are a semi-outdoor bathroom and a spacious, private area · the decor is minimalist loft, playing with exposed concrete walls, high ceilings, warm-toned wood furniture, and a beanbag lounge corner, for a feel that's simple and clean but not cold · every room has air conditioning, hot water, a flat-screen TV, a safe, tea and coffee, and a private bathroom with a shower · real guest reviews agree that the rooms are spacious, clean, and the balcony view is the real deal and the best value of all, with many saying that just sipping coffee on the balcony in the morning makes the stay worth it · a small note some people raise is that a few bathroom details, like towel hooks or shelving, aren't as complete as they'd like — a minor thing that doesn't affect the overall picture

Facilities and the pool — the most talked-about highlight of De Capoc is the saltwater infinity-edge pool, set on the hillside so the pool edge stretches out to meet the mountains and the wind turbines in the distance · early morning and evening are the popular times for guests to soak and take photos, because the light is lovely and on some days there's drifting mist · the saltwater system is gentler on the skin and eyes than a typical chlorine pool, a detail many people like · beyond the pool, the resort also has a café, a semi-outdoor restaurant, a garden, a terrace lounge, room service, a small meeting room, luggage storage, laundry service, and free Wi-Fi · parking is easy, with free private parking for about 20 cars, handy for people who drive up themselves · to be honest, the facilities here aren't extensive like a big resort's — there's no serious fitness center or full-service spa · but what's there is designed to fit the concept of resting quietly amid the view, which matches what people choose this place for · for families with small children, keep a close eye around the infinity-edge pool and the sloping ground

Food and the café — De Capoc has a semi-outdoor restaurant and café serving homemade and fusion-style food, with a relaxed setting that catches the mountain breeze · breakfast is something many reviews praise, saying the flavors are done well and the food is plated with care — not a big buffet but quality per dish · what makes eating here special is the view, since you can look out at the mountains while you eat, especially at breakfast when some days have drifting mist · for other meals, since the Thung Samo area doesn't have as dense a cluster of restaurants as the town, many people choose to eat at the resort or drive out to find places around Khao Kho–Khaem Son, which aren't far · the café here is also a spot to sip coffee and chill all day, suited to people who came to rest unhurried · overall, food at De Capoc isn't something you come specifically to eat, but it's a well-done complement that blends with the restful atmosphere · anyone who's a picky eater or wants a wide range of food options should plan to head out to places nearby as well

Service — service is another point that gets steady praise in real reviews · because it's a small resort, the staff can look after guests thoroughly and warmly, and many reviews say the team is helpful, can answer questions about routes and sights around Khao Kho, and keeps things smooth from check-in to check-out · on booking platforms the service score is high, reflecting that this attentiveness is one of the resort's strengths · check-in is 3:00 PM and check-out is around 11:00–11:30 AM · one thing worth knowing is that, since this is a small mountain stay, if you arrive late or off-hours you should let them know in advance so the team can be ready to welcome you · overall, service is a point that makes many guests say they'd come back

Real guest reviews (both praise and gripes) — gathered from Trip.com, Agoda, and Thai travel review sites, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the mountain and wind-turbine view from the rooms and the pool is the star everyone mentions, the saltwater infinity pool is beautiful and gentle on the skin, the rooms are spacious and clean with photogenic loft design, the atmosphere is quiet and good for genuine rest, the staff service is good and warm, and breakfast is tastier than expected for a stay this size · On the note side: what comes up is that prices rise quite noticeably in the cool season and on long holidays, with some feeling peak rates are high relative to the facilities on offer, that a few bathroom details like towel hooks aren't complete, that the shared facilities aren't extensive because the focus is simplicity and quiet, and that the road up is a mountain road you have to drive carefully · these gripes are mostly about setting your expectations right for the concept of a small, view-focused resort, rather than problems that keep people from returning
"Clean room, lovely design, the balcony view is the real deal · the only gripe is we came on a long holiday and the price went up a fair bit, but for a view like this it's fine."

Price comparison and value — the starting rate for a Deluxe room is about THB 2,000/night in the regular season, and can climb to around THB 2,800–4,300 in high season or on long holidays · suites and the 60-sqm Villa run from around THB 4,000 up depending on size and timing · compared with the heavily themed resorts on Khao Kho at similar prices but crowded and open to day visitors, De Capoc feels good value in terms of quiet, privacy, and design · what makes it most worth it is the mountain and wind-turbine view you get from the rooms and the pool, something money struggles to buy at a resort of the same price that isn't in this location · if you're planning a Khao Kho trip to rest quietly, take nice photos, and use the resort as a base for Wat Pha Sorn Kaew and the wind-turbine field, the money you spend pays you back in full · but if the goal is lots of activities or every amenity, you may want to also compare the big resorts in the Khaem Son area

What to know before booking — a few things help the stay go more smoothly · one, if the view matters to you, request a room facing the mountains and the wind-turbine field right when you book, because that's the main selling point here · two, the period with the coolest weather and the best chance of catching a sea of mist is late rainy to early cool season, around November to January, which is high season when rooms fill up fast and prices rise, so book several weeks ahead · three, bring warm clothes, because nights and early mornings on Khao Kho are genuinely cold · four, since this is a small mountain stay, getting here mostly requires a private car, and the final stretch is a mountain road you should drive carefully · five, compare prices across platforms and choose free cancellation up front if your plans aren't firm, because peak rates change fast · six, if you arrive outside normal check-in hours, let the resort know in advance so they can be ready to welcome you

Verdict — from all the real reviews, De Capoc Resort is the resort that suits people who want to rest quietly on Khao Kho, in a beautifully designed stay where the mountain and wind-turbine view is the star · the saltwater infinity pool, minimalist loft rooms with 180-degree view balconies, the calm atmosphere, and the location near Wat Pha Sorn Kaew make it a fitting choice for couples, photo lovers, and small families · if you're looking for a big resort with activities and every amenity, or a stay you can reach easily by public transport, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a larger resort in the Khaem Son area instead · but for a Khao Kho trip where you want quiet, design, and a memorable view at a price that's still within reach — De Capoc fits those needs neatly, and it's the reason so many reviewers say they'd come back

honestSummary: De Capoc Resort is best for people who want to rest quietly on Khao Kho, in a beautifully designed resort where the mountain and wind-turbine view is the star — a saltwater infinity pool, minimalist loft rooms with 180-degree view balconies, and a location near Wat Pha Sorn Kaew · but you have to accept that it's a small resort where the facilities aren't extensive, and prices rise noticeably in the cool season
honestChecks: If you want a big resort with lots of activities — this is a small resort of around 34 rooms focused on simplicity and quiet, with no serious fitness center or full-service spa → if you want full facilities, also consider a larger resort in the Khaem Son area

If you're not driving yourself — Khao Kho is mountain country with limited public transport, and the final stretch is a mountain road → you should rent a car or have a private one, and avoid going up at night or in heavy rain if you don't know the road well

If you want the sea of mist and cool weather — you need to come in the late-rainy-to-early-cool season (November–January), when good-view rooms fill up fast and prices rise → book several weeks ahead, request a room facing the mountains, and lock in free cancellation up front

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — De Capoc Resort Khao Kho

faq.q: Where is De Capoc Resort · what's nearby?
faq.a: It's at 254 Moo 4, Thung Samo, Khao Kho district, Phetchabun 67270, on a hillside overlooking the mountains and the wind-turbine field · about 1 km from Wat Thung Samo and about 1.5–2 km from Wat Phra That Pha Sorn Kaew · about 15–25 min drive from the Khao Kho wind-turbine field and Khao Kho Palace · about 1 hour from Phetchabun town

faq.q: What's De Capoc Resort's starting price · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 2,000/night for a Deluxe room (~42 sqm with a 180° mountain-view balcony) · there are suites like the Deluxe King Suite and Suite with Terrace, and a Villa at ~60 sqm with a semi-outdoor bathroom · prices rise in the cool season and on long holidays to around THB 2,800–4,300, so compare several platforms before booking

faq.q: Who is De Capoc Resort best for?
faq.a: It's great for couples, photo lovers, and small families who want to rest quietly in a minimalist-loft resort with a mountain and wind-turbine view · it suits people who use the resort as a base for Wat Pha Sorn Kaew and the Khao Kho sights · if you want a big resort with lots of activities or full facilities, a resort in the Khaem Son area may suit you better

It's a saltwater infinity-edge pool, set on the hillside so the pool edge meets the mountains and the wind-turbine field · prettiest in the early morning and evening, with drifting mist on some days · the saltwater system is gentler on the skin and eyes than a typical chlorine pool · families with small children should keep a close eye, since it's an infinity-edge pool on sloping ground

faq.q: When is the best time to come · will I see a sea of mist?
faq.a: The best time is late rainy to early cool season (November–January), with cool weather and a chance of a sea of mist drifting over the valley · waking early to swim or sit on the balcony for the view is most worth it · in this period good-view rooms fill up fast and prices rise, so book several weeks ahead and bring warm clothes

faq.q: How do I get to De Capoc Resort?
faq.a: Most people travel by private car or rental, since Khao Kho is mountain country with limited public transport · from Bangkok it's about a 5–6 hour drive, and about 1 hour up from Phetchabun town · the final stretch is a mountain road with steep grades and bends, so drive carefully and avoid going up at night or in heavy rain if you don't know the road well
